title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
prompt: Given two sorted arrays `nums1` and `nums2` of size `m` and `n` respectively, return the median of the two sorted arrays combined. The overall run time complexity should be `O(log(m + n))`.

examples.explanation: The merged array is [1,2,3], and its median is 2.
The merged array is [1,2,3,4], and its median is (2+3)/2 = 2.5.
One array can be empty; the median is then just the median of the other array.

hints: Merging both arrays and taking the middle element(s) works in O(m + n), but the O(log(m+n)) requirement means you shouldn't touch every element.

The median splits the combined array into two halves of equal (or near-equal) size, so think of this as searching for a partition point in the smaller array that induces a matching partition in the larger array.

Binary search over the partition index in the smaller array: for each candidate, compute the corresponding partition in the other array so the left parts together hold exactly half the total elements, then check whether every element on the left side is <= every element on the right side.

solution.approach: Always binary search over the smaller array to keep the range small. For a candidate partition index i in the shorter array, the corresponding partition j in the longer array is forced by the requirement that the left side holds exactly half (or half rounded up) of all elements combined. A valid partition is one where the max of the left side is <= the min of the right side on both arrays; if not, shift the partition left or right based on which side is out of order. Once a valid partition is found, the median comes directly from the four boundary elements (adjusted for odd/even total length), all in O(log(min(m, n))) time.
